```{r, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
```

## Translate Highcharts options to R

Tom Bishop's legend example shows how to read the Highcharts API from R.
Start with the monthly temperatures of three cities.

```{r}
library(highcharter)

data("citytemp")

hc <- highchart() |> 
  hc_xAxis(categories = citytemp$month) |> 
  hc_add_series(
    name = "Tokyo", data = citytemp$tokyo
    ) |> 
  hc_add_series(
    name = "London", data = citytemp$london
    ) |> 
  hc_add_series(
    name = "Other city",
    data = (citytemp$tokyo + citytemp$london)/2
    )

hc
```

The JavaScript legend below places the entries inside the chart and underlines
the title. In R, the top-level option becomes `hc_legend()` and each nested
object becomes a named list. Keep the option names in camel case.
[Highcharts legend options](https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/legend).

```js
legend: {
  layout: 'vertical', align: 'left', verticalAlign: 'top', floating: true,
  x: 70, y: 30,
  title: { text: 'Cities', style: { textDecoration: 'underline' } }
}
```

```{r translate-legend}
hc |>
  hc_legend(
    layout = "vertical", align = "left", verticalAlign = "top", floating = TRUE,
    x = 70, y = 30,
    title = list(text = "Cities", style = list(textDecoration = "underline"))
  )
```

## Chart

With `hc_chart` you can define general chart options.

```{r}
hc |> 
  hc_chart(
    borderColor = '#EBBA95',
    borderRadius = 10,
    borderWidth = 2,
    backgroundColor = list(
      linearGradient = c(0, 0, 500, 500),
      stops = list(
        list(0, 'rgb(255, 255, 255)'),
        list(1, 'rgb(200, 200, 255)')
        )
      )
    )
```

Now change type to column and add 3d effect.

```{r}
hc <- hc |> 
  hc_chart(
    type = "column",
    options3d = list(
      enabled = TRUE, 
      beta = 15,
      alpha = 15
      )
    )
hc

# back to the line!
hc <- hc_chart(hc, type = "line", options3d = list(enabled = FALSE))
```

## Title, subtitle, caption and credits

A good chart always have at least title, right? Then you can do it better adding relevant information
using a subtitle or caption, even link to the source of data:

```{r}
hc |> 
  hc_title(
    text = "This is the title of the chart"
    ) |> 
  hc_subtitle(
    text = "This is an intereseting subtitle to give
    context for the chart or some interesting fact"
    ) |> 
  hc_caption(
    text = "This is a long text to give some 
    subtle details of the data which can be relevant to the reader. 
    This is usually a long text that's why I'm trying to put a 
    <i>loooooong</i> text.", 
    useHTML = TRUE
    ) |> 
  hc_credits(
    text = "Chart created using R and highcharter",
    href = "http://jkunst.com/highcharter",
    enabled = TRUE
    )
```

## Axis

Usually is desirable get control or modify the behavior of the axis:

```{r}
hc |> 
  hc_xAxis(
    title = list(text = "Month in x Axis"),
    opposite = TRUE
    ) |> 
  hc_yAxis(
    title = list(text = "Temperature <b>in y Axis</b>", useHTML = TRUE),
    opposite = TRUE,
    minorTickInterval = "auto",
    minorGridLineDashStyle = "LongDashDotDot",
    showFirstLabel = FALSE,
    showLastLabel = FALSE
  )
```

A good feature is `plotLines` and `plotBand` which you can use in both axis. For example:

```{r}
hc |> 
  hc_xAxis(
    plotLines = list(
      list(
        label = list(text = "This is a plotLine"),
        color = "#FF0000",
        width = 2,
        value = 4,
        # the zIndex is used to put the label text over the grid lines 
        zIndex = 1
        )
      )
    ) |> 
  hc_yAxis(
    plotBands = list(
      list(
        from = 20,
        to = 50,
        color = hex_to_rgba("red", 0.1),
        label = list(text = "This is a plotBand"),
        # the zIndex is used to put the label text over the grid lines 
        zIndex = 1
        )
      )
    ) 
```

### Category order

Order the counts first, then pass their names and values in the same order.
Here the categories run from the most to the least common cylinder count.

```{r category-order}
counts <- sort(table(mtcars$cyl), decreasing = TRUE)

highchart() |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = names(counts), title = list(text = "Cylinders")) |>
  hc_add_series(type = "column", name = "Cars", data = as.numeric(counts))
```

For another common adjustment, see [Keep other series visible on hover](#keep-other-series-visible-on-hover).

### Four panels with their own axes

Plot vehicle weight against fuel economy in `mtcars`. Each column is a
transmission (`am`), each row an engine shape (`vs`). Give the matching X and
Y axes the same panel bounds and bind each series to the pair. All four panels
use the same scales so their points can be compared directly.

```{r four-panels}
groups <- expand.grid(am = 0:1, vs = 0:1)
panels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(groups)), function(i) {
  list(left = if (groups$am[i] == 0) "0%" else "58%",
       top = if (groups$vs[i] == 0) "0%" else "58%",
       width = "42%", height = "36%", offset = 0, lineWidth = 1,
       tickWidth = 1, tickLength = 4, tickColor = "#45545d",
       lineColor = "#45545d", labels = list(enabled = TRUE, step = 1, style = list(width = "30px", textOverflow = "clip")),
       startOnTick = FALSE, endOnTick = FALSE, showFirstLabel = TRUE, showLastLabel = TRUE,
       title = list(text = NULL))
})
x_axes <- lapply(panels, function(p) c(p, list(min = 1, max = 6, tickPositions = 2:5)))
y_axes <- lapply(panels, function(p) c(p, list(min = 8, max = 36,
                                              tickPositions = c(10, 20, 30))))
grid <- highchart() |>
  hc_chart(alignTicks = FALSE, animation = FALSE, margin = c(60, 22, 60, 38)) |>
  hc_title(text = "Weight and fuel economy") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Columns: automatic / manual. Rows: V-shaped / straight.") |>
  hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
  hc_xAxis(x_axes) |>
  hc_yAxis(y_axes)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(groups))) {
  cars <- mtcars[mtcars$am == groups$am[i] & mtcars$vs == groups$vs[i], ]
  grid <- hc_add_series(grid, cars, "scatter", hcaes(wt, mpg),
                        name = paste("am", groups$am[i], "vs", groups$vs[i]),
                        xAxis = i - 1L, yAxis = i - 1L, marker = list(symbol = "circle"))
}
grid
```

## Legend & tooltip

```{r}
hc |>
  hc_legend(
    align = "left",
    verticalAlign = "top",
    layout = "vertical",
    x = 0, y = 100
    ) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    crosshairs = TRUE,
    backgroundColor = "#F0F0F0",
    shared = TRUE, 
    borderWidth = 5
    )
```

### Keep other series visible on hover

Move the pointer over a city to inspect it. An inactive opacity of one keeps
the other cities visible at full strength for comparison.

```{r inactive-series}
hc |> hc_plotOptions(series = list(states = list(inactive = list(opacity = 1))))
```

### Markers and tooltips

A scatter series can use the same SVG for its markers and its tooltip. Save
the [R icon](icons/r-project.svg) and [Python icon](icons/python.svg) in an
`icons/` directory alongside the HTML page. These brand icons come from
[Font Awesome Free 6.7.2](https://github.com/FortAwesome/Font-Awesome/tree/6.7.2/svgs/brands)
and are licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

```{r svg-markers}
r_icon <- "./icons/r-project.svg"
python_icon <- "./icons/python.svg"

highchart() |>
  hc_title(text = "Simulated task times") |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = c("Read", "Transform", "Plot")) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Seconds")) |>
  hc_chart(type = "scatter") |>
  hc_add_series(
    name = "R", data = c(2, 4, 3), custom = list(icon = r_icon),
    marker = list(symbol = paste0("url(", r_icon, ")"), width = 20, height = 20)
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    name = "Python", data = c(3, 2, 4), custom = list(icon = python_icon),
    marker = list(symbol = paste0("url(", python_icon, ")"), width = 20, height = 20)
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(
    useHTML = TRUE,
    pointFormat = paste0("<img src='{series.options.custom.icon}' width='16' height='16' alt=''/> ",
                         "{series.name}: <b>{point.y} s</b>")
  )
```

To count units with symbols or fill a silhouette, see
[Seats and occupancy in the series gallery](series-gallery.html#seats-and-occupancy).
